user.title: Add Shark IQ Vacuum
user.description: Add one Shark IQ vacuum at a time. Run this flow again to add more vacuums. Assign each vacuum a static IP in your router first.

data.name: Name (e.g. Downstairs Shark)
data.mapping: Mapping (leave default unless you know otherwise)

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the vacuum at that IP. Make sure it's on and on the same network.
error.unknown: Unexpected error talking to the vacuum. Check Home Assistant logs.

init.title: Shark IQ Vacuum options
init.description: Tell the integration what kind of Shark this is, so it offers only the settings your robot has. Not sure? Laser-navigating robots have a round turret on top; the model number is on the sticker under the robot.

data_description.robot_type: Decides which settings and cleaning modes are offered.
data_description.scan_interval: Fallback polling; status is pushed live over MQTT. 5–600 seconds.

clean_rooms.name: Clean rooms
clean_rooms.description: Cleans the named rooms from the robot's map. Unlike Clean area, this can request a Matrix Clean.

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.description: Room names as shown in the SharkClean app (case and punctuation are ignored). The vacuum's rooms attribute lists them.

matrix.name: Matrix Clean
matrix.description: Clean the rooms twice, in a crosshatch.

clean_spot.name: Clean spot
clean_spot.description: Spot-cleans a square of about 1.5 m around a point on the robot's map.

options.lidar: Laser-navigating robot (e.g. Matrix, AI) — most models
options.spot_lidar: Compact laser robot without spot cleaning (RV2100)
options.map: Camera-navigating robot with a saved map
options.air: Camera-navigating robot without a saved map
